dossier.public_summary: The dip is not steady: it is twice as deep in one sector as the next and one of four recorded transits is almost missing, which a planet would not do. The 70% odd-even difference and very noisy Gaia astrometry show the light is from a close eclipsing binary on or near the target, not a planet.

reasons.why: Depth changes by 97% between sectors - far beyond errors - real change not a calibration offset.
reasons.value: p_constant=7.404e-7 depth_change_pct=97.1 sector56=2532 ppm sector83=877 ppm

reasons.why: Variation is within the same light-curve product, so not a pipeline calibration difference but a genuine physical change in the dip.
Individual transits are inconsistent: one is missing at 189 ppm while the others are ~1700-2500 ppm, inconsistent with a repeating planet.
reasons.value: p_consistent=1.2480192615819958e-09 chi2=44.38843693460493 dof=3 one transit 189 ppm sigma=-5.4 share_of_top_3=0.997

reasons.why: Odd/even depths differ and one sector shows >3 sigma difference, supporting a binary at twice the period rather than a single planet depth.
Gaia astrometry shows high excess noise and RUWE and multi-peak image, signs the target is itself a blended binary/eclipsing system.
